subject: science
title: Rocks
description: Comparing and grouping rocks by their appearance and properties, how fossils are formed, and how soil is made from rocks and organic matter.

objectives.statement: Compare and group together different kinds of rocks on the basis of their appearance and simple physical properties.
Describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock.
Recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter.

items.prompt: Name one property you could use to compare two rocks.
items.answer: Any of: hardness, colour, whether it is shiny or dull, whether it lets water through

items.prompt: A rock that lets water soak into it is described as...

items.statement: All rocks are exactly the same hardness.
Some rocks are hard and used for buildings, while others are soft and crumble easily.

items.prompt: To test which of two rocks is harder, you could...
options: see which one scratches the other

items.prompt: Why is a hard, waterproof rock like granite good for building?
items.answer: It is strong and does not let water soak in, so it lasts a long time
acceptableAnswers: it is hard and lasts a long time

items.prompt: Chalk is a soft rock. What happens if you rub it along the ground?
options: it leaves a mark and wears away

items.answer: The remains or shape of a living thing that lived long ago, preserved in rock
acceptableAnswers: the remains of a dead animal or plant in rock
the shape of an old living thing in rock

items.prompt: Fossils are usually found inside which of these?
Which of these best describes how a fossil forms?
options: an animal is trapped in rock and its shape is preserved over a very long time
an animal turns to stone in a few days
a rock grows legs and moves
a plant is painted onto a rock

items.statement: Fossils can teach us about animals and plants that lived millions of years ago.
Fossils form very quickly, in just a few hours.

items.prompt: What is the name of a scientist who studies fossils?
Which part of an animal is most likely to become a fossil?

items.answer: Tiny pieces of rock mixed with organic matter (rotted plants and animals)
acceptableAnswers: broken up rock and rotted plants

items.prompt: What is the name for the rotted plant and animal material found in soil?
Where do the tiny pieces of rock in soil come from?
options: larger rocks broken down over a long time
they fall from the sky as rain

items.statement: Soil contains pieces of broken-down rock.
Soil is made only of water and nothing else.

items.prompt: Why is soil important for plants?
options: it gives their roots somewhere to grow and holds water and nutrients
plants do not need soil for anything
